title: The Lost World: Jurassic Park
tagline: Site B was meant to stay off limits. So was the fridge.
about: Four years after the park disaster, Ian Malcolm is sent to a second island where the dinosaurs have been living wild.

    StartersBeach picnic roast beef finger sandwichesRare roast beef and rocket on white bread with horseradish butter, cut into fingersHow to make it40g butter, softened2 tbsp horseradish cream8 slices of white sandwich bread300g rare roast beef, thinly sliced50g rocketblack pepper, to tasteBeat the butter with the horseradish until smooth.Spread over all 8 slices of bread. Layer 4 slices with the beef, rocket and a grind of pepper and close with the rest.Trim off the crusts and cut each sandwich into 3 fingers.Ajay's spiced potato samosasCrisp pastry triangles of potato and peas with cumin, garam masala and green chilli, with mint yoghurtHow to make it200g plain flour5 tbsp vegetable oil, 3 for the dough, 2 for the filling80ml water500g potatoes, diced small1 tsp cumin seeds1 onion, finely diced1 green chilli, finely chopped1 tsp garam masala1/2 tsp ground turmeric100g frozen peas1 lemon1 bunch coriander, chopped1 L vegetable oil, for frying200g Greek yoghurt1 bunch mintsalt, to tasteRub the 3 tbsp dough oil into the flour and a pinch of salt, add the water and knead to a firm smooth dough. Cover and rest.Boil the potatoes in salted water until just tender and drain.Fry the cumin seeds in the 2 tbsp filling oil until they pop, add the onion and chilli and soften. Stir in the garam masala, turmeric, potato and peas, then a squeeze of lemon, the coriander and salt.Spread out and cool the filling.Roll the dough into 6 thin rounds and cut each in half. Fold each half into a cone, fill, wet the edge and press to seal.Heat the frying oil in a deep pot to 170°C.Fry the samosas in batches for 5 minutes, turning, until golden and blistered. Drain.Chop the mint, stir it through the yoghurt with salt and serve with the samosas.Fish tacos with lime cremaGrabbed before the rex hits the video store.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsSan Diego waterfront carne asadaCitrus and garlic marinated skirt steak, charred and sliced, with charred tomato salsa, avocado and warm corn tortillasHow to make it800g beef skirt steak1 orange, juiced3 limes, 2 for the marinade, 1 for the salsa4 garlic cloves1 tsp ground cumin1 tsp chilli powder3 tbsp vegetable oil1 bunch coriander4 ripe tomatoes1/2 white onion1 jalapeño12 small corn tortillas1 avocadosalt, to tasteBlend the orange juice, juice of 2 limes, garlic, cumin, chilli powder, oil, half the coriander and a good pinch of salt.Pour over the steak, turn to coat and marinate in the fridge.Char the tomatoes, onion and jalapeño in a dry heavy pan until blackened in patches.Blitz with the rest of the coriander, the juice of the last lime and salt to a rough salsa.Heat a grill or heavy pan until very hot. Grill the steak for 4 minutes a side.Rest the steak, loosely covered.Warm the tortillas in a dry pan and slice the avocado.Slice the steak thinly across the grain and serve with the tortillas, avocado and salsa.Roland Tembo's hunters' camp chicken curryThe great white hunter who only came to Isla Sorna for the buck rexHow to make it800g chicken thigh fillets2 tbsp vegetable oil2 brown onions3 garlic cloves20g ginger2 tbsp curry powder400g tinned crushed tomatoes400g potatoes300g basmati rice4 chapatis4 tbsp lime pickle1 corianderFry the sliced onions in the oil for 8 minutes, then the grated garlic, ginger and curry powder for 1 minute.Add the diced chicken, diced potato, tomatoes and 250ml water and simmer for 30 minutes until the potato is tender.Simmer the rice with 600ml water, covered, for 12 minutes, then rest for 5.Warm the chapati in a dry pan.Scatter the curry with coriander and serve with rice, chapati and lime pickle.SweetsRex parents' mud pieChocolate biscuit base under a dense baked dark chocolate filling, with softly whipped creamHow to make it250g chocolate biscuits250g butter, 100g melted for the base, 150g for the filling200g dark chocolate, chopped3 eggs150g brown sugar2 tbsp cocoa powder350ml thickened cream, 150ml for the filling, 200ml to whipCrush the biscuits to fine crumbs, mix with the melted base butter and press firmly into a 23cm springform tin.Chill the base. Heat the oven to 160°C.Melt the chocolate with the filling butter over low heat.Whisk the eggs and brown sugar until thick, then whisk in the chocolate, cocoa and 150ml of the cream.Pour onto the base and bake until set at the edges with a slight wobble.Cool in the tin.Chill until firm.Whip the rest of the cream to soft peaks and serve with wedges of pie.DrinksBackyard pool blue margaritaTequila and blue orange liqueur shaken with fresh lime and sugar syrup, in a salt-rimmed glassHow to make it40g caster sugar40ml hot water6 limes, juiced to make 120ml2 tbsp sea salt flakes180ml tequila60ml blue curaçao liqueur3 cups iceStir the sugar into the hot water until dissolved.Cool the syrup.Juice the limes. Rub the rims of 4 glasses with a squeezed lime half and dip in the salt.Shake the tequila, blue curaçao, lime juice and syrup hard with half the ice.Strain into the glasses over the rest of the ice.Iced tea with lemonSipped on the dock as the Venture drifts in.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
